kyo_001: You can recognise it by its trunk running almost flat and horizontal rather than climbing upward, above the stone steps. It stands between Yoshimine-dera's main hall and its pagoda.
kyo_002: You can recognise it by its trunk and branches clipped into the shape of a sailing ship, bow pointed west. It stands beside the Kyoko-chi pond at Kinkaku-ji.
kyo_003: You can recognise it by its shape, trained to echo the cone of Mount Mikami, framed through the temple hall's doorway. It stands in the garden of Hosen-in, Ohara.
kyo_004: You can recognise it by its low, wide shape, heavy branches spreading close to the ground before the trunk narrows above them. It stands in front of Nishi Honganji's Goeido Hall.
kyo_005: You can recognise it by its cascading pale pink canopy, floodlit most nights in bloom season. It stands at the centre of Maruyama Park.
kyo_006: You can recognise it as the oldest and largest tree in Kyoto Gyoen. It stands at Munakata Shrine, in the park's southwest corner.
kyo_007: You can recognise it by its canopy, 23.5 metres wide, visible from the surrounding streets before the shrine buildings themselves. It stands at Imakumano Shrine.
kyo_008: You can recognise it by its cascading weeping form, the subject of the painter Okumura Togyu's work Daigo. It stands in the garden of Sanboin, Daigo-ji.
kyo_010: You can recognise it by its white weeping blossom, standing beside the deep red flowers of its companion tree Saio-zakura. It stands between Kamigamo Shrine's first and second torii.
